gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Nippo stands tall in rope-thin outline, its small letters nearly capital-sized and no thick or thin parts anywhere. Noto Sans Coptic sits beside it as a plain sans, its middle zone full and its mouths open, so the two feel crisp and relaxed together.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Nippo draws a monoline skeleton, wire-cut and technical, with lowercase that stands almost as tall as its capitals. Noto Sans Cuneiform is the plain sans here, rounder and puffier, its open e swelling like glass beads where the heading stays lean.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Nippo's wire-cut strokes hold one gentle line thickness, and its lowercase stands almost as tall as capitals. And Noto Sans Deseret, a sans-serif with open apertures and a wide, squat-ascender lowercase, makes the whole pair feel approachable.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-devanagari: Letters traced with a single marker, small yet nearly capital-height, give Nippo its look. And Noto Sans Devanagari, a sans-serif with an open-curved g and a compact skyline, handles the quiet running text while the heading draws attention.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Technical and wire-sharp, Nippo shows zero stroke modulation. Noto Sans Duployan, a sans-serif with a wide-mouthed a and oversized e counters, would carry a longer passage with generous, easygoing openness under that tight heading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Nippo's steady, pressure-free line looks cut from wire. Noto Sans Elbasan, a sans-serif with large lowercase and open terminals, gives the pair its strongest quality: a crisp heading over a body that never pinches.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic reads open and unhurried throughout. Nippo, with no hairlines anywhere and wire-cut strokes, sits above it as a crisp, technical heading, while the sans body keeps the text quietly accessible.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Modern and sturdy, this pair splits its work cleanly. Nippo's wire-cut letters have no thick-thin swing at all, while Noto Sans Ethiopic, a sans-serif with tall lowercase and far-hanging c terminals, gives the pairing its strongest quality: sturdiness.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Nippo looks like a bent paperclip, with no thick-thin shifts and small letters nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Georgian, a sans with open curves and short ascender stems, gives the pair its strongest quality: tidy, modern contrast.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Thin, wire-cut and technical, Nippo draws bowls and stems at the same weight, with lowercase almost capital-tall. Make it small beside Noto Sans Glagolitic, a sans-serif with sturdy open rounds, and it loses presence.
